subject: Data filename and read in order and its relationship with Group column in `covar` subject info

messages.author: 638777fa743438d8
messages.subject: Data filename and read in order and its relationship with Group column in `covar` subject info
parts:
Hi Chris, 

I'm loading up a complex study design with many data file that spans over multiple groups in `covar`. I did not follow what you have in Chap7 where you separated groups into different subfolders but rather located them in 1 single folder. 

If that's how I structured my data files, is it correct that the rows of the Group column in my `covar` dataframe should match the order of files from what `list.files` listed? Such that `inds` could generate a correct cluster index for each different filename row to the Groups I have in `covar`? 

Now in your program, is there any mechanism that you are matching (ie. grepping) any parts for the filenames from `list.files` from that of the Study.ID column in `covar`? Or you are assuming in our `covar` dataframe the order for each Study.ID should also match the `list.files` file orders?

Thanks for your confirmation!

Sean

messages.author: dadcb4fd6a01f8d1
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Data filename and read in order and its relationship with Group column in `covar` subject info
parts:
Hi Sean, sorry for not replying earlier.

Yes, you certainly are not required to split subject groups into separate directories (in fact, I do not for other projects). I mention this "off-handedly" in the footnote, but can be more explicit when I next update the Guide.
For that case (all data in a single directory), I create "inds" as follows:

setkey(covars.dti, Study.ID)
inds <- lapply(seq_along(groups), function(x) covars.dti[, which(Group == groups[x])])

I have the covariate table sorted by "Study.ID", in alphanumeric order by default; this is the same as it is ordered on the filesystem as well, because the filenames (e.g., the "fdt_network_matrix" files for "probtrackx2" output) begin with the Study ID's. So yes, you will have to be sure that the data in "covars" is correct; e.g., that sub01 is truly a "Control", sub02 is truly a "Patient", sub03 is truly a "Patient", and so on.

----
To show a concrete example, for one project the Study ID's (and therefore the filenames) are as follows:

01-196-7_fdt_network_matrix
01-062-8_fdt_network_matrix
01-093-2_fdt_network_matrix
01-117-3_fdt_network_matrix
01-255-0_fdt_network_matrix
etc.

This is the order that was in my original "covars.csv" file; I believe this is because Study.ID's were assigned pseudo-randomly, and not in order of study recruitment (or MRI acquisition). So ultimately I had to make sure that the "Group" was correct for each of the subjects (and, of course, the rest of the variables). It later turned out for that study that one of the subjects was included erroneously, and belonged to a different project altogether. Basically, housekeeping is of paramount importance, and it is best if you have (an) amazing study coordinator(s).

There is no "grepping" that is done in brainGraph; I didn't want to impose such a requirement, even if I can't imagine other ways researchers would name their data files and create their Study.ID's. I suppose it would cause problems if there are spaces or special characters in the ID's and/or filenames; of course neither of which is recommended.

I hope this answers your question (and isn't an information overload!). Please let me know if you have follow-up questions.

Chris
